summary:
Lunar Navigator is an interactive lunar landing site and mission window explorer developed by The Starseekers

Choosing when and where to operate on the Moon requires understanding sunlight, terrain shadows and visibility of Earth. These conditions are particularly challenging near the lunar south pole, where even nearby locations can experience different illumination conditions

Our application combines NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter terrain and imagery with JPL-derived astronomical data. Users can select locations and dates, explore lunar terrain, observe the Sun and Earth from the surface, inspect their positions against the surrounding horizon and compare alternative scenarios

Linked 3D, map, surface sky and timeline views make complex scientific geometry easier to interpret. The application also identifies where incomplete terrain measurements limit visibility predictions

Lunar Navigator aims to make lunar environmental analysis more accessible to students, educators and early-stage mission planners, while preserving the distinction between calculated conditions and engineering assumptions
details:
### What we built

Lunar Navigator is an interactive application for examining sunlight, Earth visibility and terrain conditions at lunar landing sites

It combines NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter elevation and imagery with JPL-derived ephemerides to calculate the positions of the Sun and Earth as seen from selected locations on the Moon

Users can explore lunar terrain, select coordinates, adjust observation times and heights, inspect the Sun and Earth relative to the local horizon, and compare alternative mission scenarios

### How it works

The astronomy engine evaluates Sun and Earth directions using precomputed SPICE-derived data. For supported south-polar sites, a separate terrain model estimates local obstructions and their timing

The interface links the 3D terrain view, Moon atlas, Surface Sky, timeline and analysis results. Time changes update the astronomical geometry, allowing users to examine how mission conditions develop

The application also includes scientific reference-frame information, documented data sources, numerical tests and explicit limits on terrain coverage

### Why it matters

Near the lunar poles, terrain and low solar elevation can substantially affect illumination and opportunities for direct-to-Earth communication

Lunar Navigator makes these conditions easier to inspect and compare without requiring users to operate several specialised scientific tools

The application distinguishes measured terrain obstruction from unknown distant obstructions. Geometric sunlight and Earth visibility do not, by themselves, establish electrical power, radio-link performance or landing safety

### Technology

JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Python, browser-based scientific workers, 2D and 3D rendering, NASA LRO/LOLA terrain products, lunar imagery, and JPL NAIF SPICE-derived astronomical data

The project was developed by The Starseekers: Averius Wan, Vincent Lee and Cayden Chan
